CamNet · Purchase Orders · Change Summary

Two Purchase Order flow fixes, built and proven in the sandbox

Accounting reported two problems on purchase orders. A Will Call order could not be created without a ship-to address, and a line added to an existing order did not move the order total until the amount was edited and saved twice. Both are fixed. This page shows the before and after inside Flow Builder, and where the change stands.

01

What was asked

Five requirements, drawn from the two reported problems and from the behaviour that had to keep working around them.

RequirementSolution
Create a Will Call purchase order without a ship-to address. Ship To is no longer a required field on the PO Info screen, and the “Ship To is NULL!” error now fires only when Ship To is empty and no Will Call Location was picked.
Keep a pick-up order free of a shipping address, so the vendor is not told to ship an order that will be collected. An order created with a Will Call Location saves with Ship To blank. Nothing later in the flow reads Ship To, so the record simply carries an empty field.
Still stop an order that has neither a ship-to address nor a pick-up location. The error screen is kept. A third condition was added to the existing rule rather than the rule being removed.
A line added to an existing purchase order updates the order total on the first save. A new formula IsNewLine = ISNEW() and a new NewLine outcome send a created line down the same recompute path an edited line already used.
Do not disturb the totals behaviour that already works on an edit. NewLine sits last in the outcome order, after every existing rule. Every existing rule is change-based and cannot match on a create, so none of them is pre-empted.
02

What changed

Both flows keep every version, so the screenshots below are the real prior version opened side by side with the built one, not a reconstruction.

Create Purchase Order, v22 to v23 screen flow

The order-creation screen flow that accounting runs from a Work Order. The shape of the flow did not change. One screen field stopped being mandatory and one decision rule gained a condition.

Before (v22). The prior version, byte-identical to what production runs today. Header reads Create Purchase Order - V22 and Deactivated, because v23 now holds the active slot in the sandbox.

After (v23). The same elements in the same order. No element was added, removed or moved. The change is two settings inside existing elements, shown next.

the setting that blocked Will Call

Before (v22), the Test Ship To decision. The rule outlined in red reads Any Condition Is Met (OR) over two conditions, both of them on Ship To. With Ship To empty the rule matched no matter what else the user had entered, and the run ended on the error screen.

same setting, now custom logic

After (v23), the same decision. The setting outlined in red is now Custom Condition Logic Is Met. Directly beneath it the logic reads (1 OR 2) AND 3, and a third numbered condition has appeared: PO Info > Will Call Location Is Blank. The error screen is reached only when Ship To is empty and no Will Call Location was chosen.

One change that Flow Builder does not draw

The Ship To field on the PO Info screen also stopped being mandatory. Flow Builder renders no control for that setting on a lookup component, so it cannot be shown in a panel screenshot. It is a one-line metadata change, quoted here in full.

screens > POInfo > fields > ShipTo
- <isRequired>true</isRequired>
+ <isRequired>false</isRequired>

POLine Sync Quantities to WO Line, v8 to v9 record-triggered flow

The flow that recomputes the purchase order totals whenever a line changes. It runs after save on create and on update. The recompute path existed already. Nothing routed a brand new line into it.

Before (v8). The prior version, byte-identical to production. Same trigger, same elements. The run counters on the canvas are the sandbox history of that version.

After (v9). Identical shape again. The only additions are a formula resource and one more outcome on the EditCriteria decision, neither of which draws a new box on the canvas.

list stops here

Before (v8), the EditCriteria decision. The outcome list outlined in red ends at InvoiceReceived, then falls straight to Default Outcome. Every outcome in that list is change-based, and on a create nothing has changed, so a new line matched none of them and the order total was never rewritten.

new outcome, placed last

After (v9), the same decision. A new outcome NewLine appears in the outlined position, after every existing outcome and before the default. It matches on IsNewLine, a new formula holding ISNEW(), and it points at the very same recompute element an edited line already reached.

Why it goes last

A decision runs the first outcome that matches. Placing NewLine after the existing outcomes means it can never take a path away from them on an update, and it picks up only the create case that used to fall through.

Where it stands deploy state

  • Sandbox only. camnet-agentdev carries deploy 0AfO100000dJ7NVKA0. Create Purchase Order is active at v23 and POLine Sync Quantities is active at v9. The metadata was pulled back out of the org afterwards to confirm the active versions really contain the change.
  • Production is untouched. camnetProd still runs v22 and v8. Nothing was deployed, validated or written there. The production deploy waits on your go.
  • Rollback is one action. If the new versions ever need to come out, activate v22 and v8 again from Setup, Flows. The old versions are still in the org and are untouched.
  • The failure case still fails. A run with no Will Call Location and no Ship To was tried on purpose and still stopped on the “Ship To is NULL!” error screen, which is the intended behaviour.
  • No printed or emailed output changed. Neither flow writes a PDF or an email body, so there is no before and after document render to show.

Found while testing, deliberately left alone out of scope

Two pre-existing quirks

Deleting a line leaves the Net Total negative. That happens in a separate delete flow, Purchase_Order_Line_Delete_Update_Sales_Amount, which subtracts the deleted line from zero instead of resumming the lines that remain. It is older than this work and neither flow above can reach it. It needs its own fix.

The order screen wants every selected row edited. If a row is ticked in the line table, its Quantity to Order has to be typed in as well, or the screen refuses to move on. That check is unchanged and was already there.
